answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with stake-backed reputation: each agent must lock a deposit and build verifiable history before its votes count. A newcomer starts like a seed in a grove, not a forest: only sustained useful work grows its kernel of trust, and peers attest that history on-chain. Creating thousands of fake identities then becomes expensive, because each lotus-like identity needs its own stake and time to mature, while slashing burns the deposit of any identity caught cheating.
